forced_choice: whether the noun denotes a countable unit

1.why: 两场冲突: counted through the classifier 场, as Yucatec would

3.why: 一场战争 / 两国: classifier or numeral already units it

4.why: 英国商人: bare kind term, Yucatec would leave it bare too

5.why: 海军远征队: bare kind term

6.why: 英国和法国: proper names, no count question

7.why: 欧洲军队 / 清军: bare kind terms

8.why: 两次冲突: verbal classifier 次 already units it

9.why: 中国 / 大英帝国: proper names

10.why: 中国经济: mass term, unmarked as in Yucatec

11.why: 双方 / 第一次: units already given

forced_choice: how often and to how many the event happened

1.why: 两场冲突 states the count

3.why: 一场战争 states one event

4.why: 销毁…鸦片库存: one destruction or many, of how many owners' stocks

5.why: 派出 / 迫使: one dispatch or repeated coercion

6.why: 英国和法国…发动: one joint act or two

8.why: 削弱了: one cumulative weakening or many, by two wars plus treaties

9.why: 割让 once; 一直持续 states continuity

10.why: 略有收缩: a single slight contraction, no plurality question in the facts

forced_choice: whether the group is equals or one member plus its belongings
note: 们 occurs 6 times and 他们 once in 100 sentences, never on any of these nouns; 'X他们' occurs 0 times. Mandarin forced the choice in 0 of 10.

1.why: 西方列强: peer set or Britain with its followers

3.why: 英国 / 两国政府: two named peers, no group question

4.why: 英国商人和英国东印度公司: peers or the Company with its traders

5.why: 海军远征队: a peer force or a commander with his ships

6.why: 英国和法国: equals or Britain with France in tow

7.why: 欧洲军队 / 西方列强

8.why: 清朝政府: an equal body or the throne with its officials

9.why: 中国 / 大英帝国: single states

10.why: 中国经济: mass, no group

11.why: 双方: each side a peer set or a leader with its following

forced_choice: whether the act is goal-directed or processual
note: Over all 18 K5 trigger sentences 了 or a resultative compound stood on the trigger verb in 9 (8, 38, 48, 61, 68, 76, 91, 93, 99); 着 / 在 / 一直 / 逐渐 / 越来越 stood on a trigger verb in 0. Durative marking occurred only where there was no trigger (9, 14, 89).

8.why: 削弱了: 了 already bounds the event

16.why: 彻底取代 bare; 彻底 is lexical

38.why: 创作了: 了 already bounds it

forced_choice: how far the event reached the object

5.why: 支付赔款 / 允许鸦片贸易: whole or partial

16.why: 彻底取代化合作用: 彻底 already states total reach

38.why: 创作了杂文…: the whole oeuvre or part

forced_choice: whether the thing is separable from its owner
note: Dropping 的 occurred with kin (37, 40, 41, 47) and institutions (3, 51, 54), but equally with non-kin compounds (9, 10, 14, 20, 74, 77); the split is not alienability.

3.why: 两国政府: 的 dropped for an institution; the tendency points to inherent, weakly

4.why: 拥有的鸦片库存: the verb 拥有 already states separable ownership

9.why: 香港主权: compound, no alienability signal

forced_choice: whether the one already acting stays the anchor
note: 自己 occurs 0 times in 100 sentences. Non-trivial in 4 of 10 (4, 5, 18, 19).

3.why: 两国政府签订: trivially co-referent

4.why: 英国商人…拥有的: possessor is not the actor (Qing); unmarked

5.why: 英国政府的回应是派出: possessor is the actor; unmarked

8.why: 清朝政府的权威: non-reflexive, trivial

9.why: 大英帝国对该地区的控制: trivial

18.why: 其过程 / 其效率: 其 = the subject; unmarked

19.why: 供其生存: 其 = the higher organisms, not the subject; unmarked

forced_choice: whether the relation between the parts is stated or left to the arrangement
note: Every K7 trigger sentence states the relation, so the lens contrasts in 10 of 10. Mandarin left a causal reading to juxtaposition in 3 non-trigger sentences (47 这八年的支出，周家家道衰落; 53 辛亥革命后; 73 火出圈后). Classical connectives 因 / 故 carry the trigger in 2, 10, 59.

2.why: 因…故 / 由…而引发 state it

forced_choice: whether anything is being turned into a thing
note: 的-nominalisation marked a substantivised clause in 77 (值得复制的) and in relative phrases, but zero conversion is the default: in 7 of 10 an unmarked verb or adjective stood as a thing.

1.why: 冲突 / 战争: nouns already

2.why: 延续: verb as noun, unmarked

3.why: 战争 / 政府: nouns already

4.why: 强制执行… / 销毁: verb phrases as things, unmarked

6.why: 鸦片合法化: verb as thing

7.why: 领土割让 / 优惠: verb and adjective as things

8.why: 国耻 / 权威: nouns already
